abstract: Analysis of the cellular origin of carcinomas of different organs indicates that there is in each instance, a determined stem cell required for tissue renewal that is the cell of origin for carcinomas. The normal tissue-determined stem cells are the result of differentiation in the embryo and are little changed, if at all, from the embryonic cells. Malignant stem cells are derived from these normal stem cells of adult tissues. The resultant tumors are caricatures of the normal process of tissue renewal with many stem cells and imperfect differentiation (14). This imparts an undifferentiated appearance to the tumors, not a dedifferentiated one. Study of the regulation of normal stem cells in the embryo should lead to rational therapies for malignant ones, and conversely, study of secretions and regulation of malignant stem cells will provide insights into normal regulation. The cancer-derived differentiated cells are benign (12, 74) if not normal (39, 53) leading to the conclusion that attempts to direct normal differentiation of malignant stem cells might serve as an alternative to cytotoxic therapy. Attempts to develop such therapies are currently underway (208). The degree of differentiation of a carcinoma depends on the proportion of undifferentiated tumor stem cells, the stage of maturation arrest of the majority of cells in the tumor, and on the ability of some cells to escape arrest and to differentiate (Fig. 1). These concepts of the stem cell contribution to tumors originated largely from studies of teratocarcinoma (209) and were not widely accepted because many considered the lessons learned were unique to teratocarcinomas and would not apply to other tissues. On the basis of the concepts covered in this review, it is clear that teratocarcinomas are unique only in the potential of their stem cells. Other stem cells have more limited potential. The balance of expression of the differentiated histiotype of the tumor cell lineage and the undifferentiated phenotype of the tumor stem cells determine the morphology of the tumor. Normal tissue renewal of epithelial organs is also from stem cells or their differentiating progeny. The cellular events during liver development and regeneration and the changes that precede the development of liver cancer during hepatocarcinogenesis are similar to the cellular response in pancreas, prostate, breast, lung, and gut. In liver, as in the leukopoietic system, the primitive tissue-specific stem cell is not primarily involved in renewal because that would be too slow a process; individuals would die before generation of sufficient replacement cells.(ABSTRACT TRUNCATED AT 400 WORDS)
abstract_ja: 各臓器の癌の細胞起源を解析すると、いずれの場合も組織の更新に必要な、決定された幹細胞が存在し、それが癌の起源となることが示される。組織決定性の正常幹細胞は胚における分化の結果であり、胚細胞からほとんど、あるいは全く変化していない。悪性幹細胞は成人組織のこれらの正常幹細胞に由来する。生じる腫瘍は、多数の幹細胞と不完全な分化を伴う正常な組織更新の戯画であり、そのため未分化な外観を呈する。これは脱分化ではなく未分化の外観である。がん由来の分化細胞は、正常でないとしても(39, 53)、良性である(12, 74)。したがって、悪性幹細胞の正常な分化を誘導する試みは、細胞傷害性治療の代替になりうるという結論に至る。そのような治療法の開発が現在進行中である(208)。腫瘍の分化度は、未分化な腫瘍幹細胞の割合、腫瘍内の大多数の細胞の成熟停止の段階、そして一部の細胞が停止を逃れて分化する能力によって決まる(図1)。これらの癌の幹細胞の寄与に関する概念は主に奇形癌の研究から生まれたが、当初は奇形癌に特有のものとみなされ、広くは受け入れられなかった。本総説の概念に照らせば、奇形癌は幹細胞の可能性においてのみ独特であり、他の幹細胞はより限られた可能性を持つ。腫瘍の形態は、腫瘍細胞系譜の分化した組織型の発現と、腫瘍幹細胞の未分化な表現型のバランスによって決まる。上皮性臓器の正常な組織更新も、幹細胞またはその分化中の子孫に由来する。肝臓の発生と再生における細胞事象、および肝発癌の過程で肝癌の発生に先立つ細胞変化は、膵臓、前立腺、乳腺、肺、腸管における細胞応答と類似している。肝臓では、白血球生成系と同様に、原始的な組織特異的幹細胞は主として更新に関与しない。そのような過程は遅すぎ、十分な数の補充細胞が生成される前に個体が死亡してしまうからである。（抄録は400語で打ち切られている）
